item.title: Shirley Horn recognized with Order of Ontario
item.description: Algoma University’s first chancellor will be awarded the Order of Ontario. Shirley Horn is one of 30 appointments to the honour that recognizes distinguished service and extraordinary achievements. “The 2025 Order of Order appointees represent the very best of our province,” said Lt.-Gov. item.description: A man’s theft of clothing for a job interview earned him some face time with a judge. John Lannigan pleaded guilty to theft under $5,000 on Tuesday. item.title: Sault man with wrench lunges at security guards
item.description: A man wielding a knife lunged at security guards at a downtown business, police say. The Feb. 11 incident followed a Feb. 2 occurrence when the same male allegedly threatened security when he was being escorted off the property. item.title: Developers, entrepreneurs sought for Pointe des Chenes former campground
item.description: The request for proposal process closes April 13 and submissions will be reviewed, with a recommendation suggested for council.

item.description: A bank card left at an ATM was allegedly used to get money by a person who found it last fall. item.title: Canada's Defence Strategy to help strengthen steel industry, including Algoma
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney launched Canada’s first Defence Industrial Strategy and that could mean more orders for Algoma steel.
